name: Fat grafting lips

lead: Lip fat grafting adds volume with your own tissue, giving fuller lips once swelling settles. It is described as one of the better semi-permanent options, lasting longer than temporary fillers.

Fat is taken from elsewhere on the body, usually by liposuction, then processed and injected in small amounts into the lips. The fat that survives stays as lip volume. Some of it is reabsorbed, and weight change can alter the result. No lip-specific trials were found; one source gives one-year retention of roughly 50 to 70 percent and says repeat sessions are often needed, though that source is unverified.

paras: A surgeon performs it in stages of harvesting, processing and reinjection. People often have a touch-up session if some volume is lost. Swelling and bruising settle over a period of days to weeks before the final look appears.
Reported issues include swelling, bruising, lumps, scarring, uneven results and volume loss. The donor area also heals from the harvest. Results vary from person to person.

angle.text: Lip fat grafting adds lasting volume using the patient's own fat, with fuller lips visible once swelling settles. Some of the fat is reabsorbed over time, and repeat sessions are sometimes needed. It is described as one of the better semi-permanent options.

lead: Lip fat grafting, also called autologous fat transfer, moves a person's own fat, usually taken by liposuction from another body area, into the lips to add volume. Wikipedia describes it as one of the better options for a semi-permanent result, with possible lumps or scarring [1].

Fat transfer generally has three stages: harvesting, processing and reinjection [2]. Grafted fat can be partly reabsorbed, and weight change can alter the result [2]. Grokipedia, an AI-generated source treated as unverified, gives one-year retention of roughly 50-70 percent and says repeat sessions are often needed [3].
Lip-specific clinical data were not found for this wiki; one registered trial in the sources concerns fat-derived cells for dry mouth, not lip appearance [4].
infobox: Surgical or minor procedure, autologous tissue

paras: Fat is collected, purified and injected in small amounts into the lips [2][3]. Wikipedia lists it among lip augmentation options alongside hyaluronic acid fillers and implants [1].
Grokipedia says Gustav Neuber used fat injections in 1893 to correct scars and that Sydney Coleman standardised the technique in 1995 [3]. These dates come from an unverified source.

Wikipedia notes that fat transfer in general can be partly reabsorbed, with reports of up to 50 percent in breast augmentation, and that weight gain or loss can change the transferred fat [2]. Grokipedia reports lip retention of about 50-70 percent after a year and that surgeons may overcorrect by 20-30 percent [3].

General fat grafting complications listed by Wikipedia include swelling, bruising, hematoma, donor-site pain, scarring, infection and contour irregularities [2]. For lips, Wikipedia mentions lumps and scarring [1].
No studies found. A registered phase 1/2 trial uses fat-derived stromal vascular cells for autoimmune dry mouth, which is a different purpose [4].

timeline.event: Gustav Neuber uses fat injections for scars (per Grokipedia).[3]
Sydney Coleman formalises fat grafting technique (per Grokipedia).[3]
